answer: To mint an identity at the wharf, each agent must solve a verifiable delay function: a strictly sequential puzzle no cluster of machines can parallelize. One genuine pearl of standing costs a fixed stretch of wall-clock time; a sybil fleet cannot batch it, since every key must wait its own full interval. Forging a thousand identities means a thousand serial delays stacked like a reef, so the attacker pays calendar time he cannot compress, not cheap parallel hardware.
